deduplication.reason: This delta adds a distinct evaluation/falsification contract for semantic anchoring versus episode-local binding; it does not duplicate existing generators, atom gates or checkpoint identity sources.

external_primary_research.source: Kumar (2025), Semantic Anchors in In-Context Learning: Why Small LLMs Cannot Flip Their Labels, arXiv:2511.21038
external_primary_research.finding: Across reported 1-12B open models, inverted demonstration semantics did not produce coherent anti-semantic classifiers; prompt alignment rose only with accuracy loss and the reported semantic override rate remained zero in the studied few-shot setting.
external_primary_research.trigger2_relevance: Qwen3.5-0.8B should not be assumed to learn arbitrary episode-local semantic remapping from prompt/codebook presence alone. Dynamic binding must be trained and separately measured against pretraining or fine-tuning semantic anchors.

external_primary_research.source: Wu, Geiger, Milliere (2025), How Do Transformers Learn Variable Binding in Symbolic Programs?, arXiv:2505.20896
external_primary_research.finding: A transformer can move from random behavior through a shallow heuristic phase to systematic dereferencing, with causal interventions identifying routing mechanisms.
external_primary_research.trigger2_relevance: Final aggregate accuracy is insufficient. Measure binding at multiple checkpoints and require orbit-level systematicity plus causal/nuisance controls.

external_primary_research.source: Peng et al. (2025), Enhancing Input-Label Mapping in In-Context Learning with Contrastive Decoding, arXiv:2502.13738
external_primary_research.finding: Input-label mapping is a distinct failure surface in ICL and can be improved independently of general semantic task competence.
external_primary_research.trigger2_relevance: Keep READ semantics, BIND_ROUTE mapping and WRITE atom emission as separate evaluation channels.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A successful Xeno binder will follow the current episode codebook even when it conflicts with any global atom-to-semantic association learned during pretraining or fine-tuning.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Fine-tuning will create stable atom semantic anchors; apparent binding gains will mostly reflect those global associations and fail under permutation reversal.
hypotheses.discriminator: For the same semantic item and same three valid one-token atoms, evaluate all six S3 codebook permutations under identical renderer structure. Require target changes to follow only the episode mapping and measure complete-orbit correctness rather than marginal accuracy.

hypotheses.hypothesis: READ and WRITE can remain strong while BIND_ROUTE fails, especially for counter-prior or unseen permutations.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Any observed binding failure is actually semantic misclassification or inability to emit the chosen atom.
hypotheses.discriminator: Use matched positive controls that separately verify semantic class readout and one-token atom emission, then score the composed BIND_ROUTE task on the same items and atoms.

activation_prerequisites: runtime quiescence proven and current execution authority re-entered
exact accepted 46-atom inventory and exact candidate tokenizer identity are bound
family/provenance holdout and nuisance-independence gates are frozen before outputs are opened
paired_units: direct and inverted query forms where semantics are unambiguous
family-disjoint unseen template and symbol partitions

primary_metrics.s3_orbit_complete_accuracy: fraction of semantic items for which all six mapping permutations are correct
primary_metrics.counter_prior_override_accuracy: accuracy restricted to mappings that oppose the candidate's empirically measured context-free or dominant atom-class prior
primary_metrics.mapping_equivariance_violation_rate: fraction of mapping permutations where target fails to transform according to the codebook permutation
primary_metrics.read_bind_write_decomposition: separate READ, BIND_ROUTE and WRITE error rates on matched units
primary_metrics.atom_prior_predictability: ability of atom identity alone, without semantic payload/codebook, to predict semantic class; promotion requires preregistered chance-compatible behavior after balancing

positive_falsifiers: inject a fixed global class-to-atom mapping into a synthetic control model or scoring rule and require the gate to reject it
remove or corrupt the episode codebook and require BIND_ROUTE performance to collapse while READ control may remain intact
permute codebook labels while holding semantic evidence fixed and require output to transform with the permutation
fail_closed_rules: Marginal accuracy cannot substitute for complete S3 orbit consistency.
A high READ score plus a high WRITE score does not mint BIND_ROUTE credit.
Natural/default mapping success cannot substitute for counter-prior override success.
No threshold may be chosen after confirmatory outputs are exposed; freeze practical margins and tie/Pareto policy prospectively.
Do not convert this evaluation design into positive training rows or checkpoint-selection credit before independent current admission gates pass.

training_reinjection.curriculum_delta: Add semantic-anchor override/counter-prior mapping as a mandatory post-training binding evaluation family once exact identity, atom, renderer, family and execution gates are open.

next_exact_action: Keep current V52 quiescence-first priority. After runtime quiescence and three-candidate identity eligibility, freeze this semantic-anchor override gate before opening a fresh family-disjoint block; then use complete S3 orbit and counter-prior override metrics to distinguish genuine episode-local binding from learned global atom semantics.
